value:
SCOPE BOUNDARY on claim.law.MV_callee-saved-numbering-has-a-width-class-ahead-of-declaration-order.20260902.v1. That law establishes that narrow (byte-typed) locals form their own callee-saved numbering class ahead of every word-sized local, and that THE ONLY LEVER ACROSS THE BOUNDARY IS THE DECLARED TYPE, AND IT IS FREE - retyping u8 to int with an explicit truncating cast moves the numbering while the instruction count, the opcode multiset and every mnemonic hold. That freeness claim is TRUE ONLY WHEN THE NARROW LOCAL'S VALUE IS CONSUMED BY A TRUNCATING OPERATION. IT IS FALSE WHEN THE NARROW LOCAL IS WIDENED INTO ANOTHER LOCAL, because the widening copy exists ONLY to change width: delete the width difference and MWCC coalesces the two locals, DELETES THE COPY, and the retype becomes COUNT-ASYMMETRIC - the one condition that puts a function outside every postprocessor class by construction.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 on game/movie/movieplayer.cpp::fn_800D8BCC at HEAD 0f45ae610. The if-branch's inner do-while declares `u8 idx; u32 val; u8* entry;` and assigns `idx = *ip; val = idx;`. Retyping to `u32 idx` with everything else held constant took the function from a count-symmetric 215/215 with a 4-token multiset to 214 vs 215 with a 5-token multiset, real 184 to 295, and additionally MOVED the extabindex section. The deleted instruction is precisely the widening copy: `addi r9,r10,0` at +0x1ec, WHICH THE TARGET HAS. So the count asymmetry is not a scoring artifact - it is the source spelling going wrong, and it identifies the target's own shape in the same measurement. `u8 idx` widened into a u32 val is what the retail compiler was fed, and the surviving asymmetric `+1 addi` in the multiset is the tell.

THE DIAGNOSTIC, which is what makes this transferable. The width-class law's cure and this law's counterexample are told apart by ONE zero-build question about the narrow local: WHERE DOES ITS VALUE GO? If every use truncates or the value is consumed in place - the sh0/sh1/sh2 shift amounts behind the parent law, each fed straight into a `sraw` - the retype is free, because the (u8) cast MWCC emits for an explicit truncation is the same `clrlwi rD,rS,24` it emits for the implicit truncation on assignment into a u8, and nothing else moves. If the value is ASSIGNED INTO A WIDER LOCAL, the copy carrying that assignment is load-bearing and the retype will delete it. Read the target for a register-to-register copy sitting between the narrow load and the wide use; if one is there, the narrow type is the target's own and the retype is not available as a lever at all.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS FUNCTION. The parent law's freeness claim is the thing that licenses a retype probe anywhere in the corpus, and a retype that silently breaks count symmetry is expensive twice over: it costs the build, and a count-asymmetric state read as a mere regression can be recorded as a weak negative when it is in fact a categorical statement about the source spelling. Quote the instruction counts as N/N on any retype probe, not just the score.
